KJV.name: King James Version (KJV)
KJV.description: The King James Version (KJV), or Authorized Version, is an English translation of the Christian Bible commissioned by King James I and published in 1611. Known for its majestic, rhythmic prose, it was created by 47 scholars using a rigorous committee-based, formal equivalence ("word-for-word") approach based on original Hebrew, Greek, and earlier English translations.

NIV.name: New International Version (NIV)
NIV.description: The New International Version (NIV) is a widely used, contemporary English translation of the Bible that balances literal accuracy with readability, often described as a "thought-for-thought" or dynamic equivalence translation. It was first published in 1978, with major revisions in 1984 and 2011, aimed at producing a clear, accurate Bible for modern readers, using recent critical editions of the original Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek texts.

ESV.name: English Standard Version (ESV)
ESV.description: The English Standard Version (ESV) is an "essentially literal" Bible translation that prioritizes "word-for-word" accuracy, balancing precise translation with contemporary readability. It captures the original Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek nuances while maintaining literary style, making it ideal for study, public reading, and personal devotions.

CPDV.name: Catholic Public Domain Version (CPDV)
CPDV.description: The Catholic Public Domain Version (CPDV) is a modern English translation of the Bible (completed 2009) by Ronald L. Conte Jr.. It is designed to be free from copyright, based on the Latin Vulgate and the Challoner Douay-Rheims version. The CPDV includes all deuterocanonical books and is designed to adhere to Roman Catholic doctrine and Vatican translation norms.

ASV.name: American Standard version  (ASV)
ASV.description: The American Standard Version (ASV) of 1901 is a highly literal, word-for-word English Bible translation, often considered a foundational "standard" for 20th-century American Protestantism. Derived from the English Revised Version (1881–1885), it updated the King James Version (KJV) to incorporate more accurate, recently discovered manuscripts.
